findings.problem: pull_request runs execute the PR's own ci.yml, grants_widening.sh, widening_gate.py, gxg_policy and uv.lock. A PR that adds a grant and sets grants_widening.sh to `exit 0` (or edits diff.py, or pins a package in uv.lock) gets green grants-widening/ci-ok on its head without the label. Documented by the executor as a known limit, but no owner decision accepting it is recorded in the plan. Five of six paths are closable in-repo; only ci.yml itself is not on this GitHub plan.
findings.required_improvement: Executor: the gate step runs grants_widening.sh, widening_gate.py and gxg-policy from a worktree of refs/remotes/origin/main (uv run --project <main>), and that main-side gate requires the label when the PR diff vs main touches ci.yml, scripts/ci/, tools/gxg-policy/, schemas/, pyproject.toml, uv.lock; job test: PR that edits the gate script or diff.py with widening -> red. Owner: record in the plan that the remaining `.github/workflows/` path is accepted (owner reads every such PR) or use an org ruleset with a required workflow.

findings.problem: Since this cycle the signed bundle takes effect_class/action/executes_via from connectors/*/gxg-manifest.yaml, and the Approval Service trusts only those (AS-26). diff reads only policies/. Reproduced: same policies, manifest demo.message.propose external_effect -> write_reversible: bundles differ, diff reports 0 widening and 0 narrowing; after merge AP-01 gives `not_required` (no human). high_risk -> external_effect falls under an existing effect_classes auto_approve rule. connectors/ is not in CODEOWNERS. Latent until the first manifest lands (M3).
findings.required_improvement: diff takes base/head manifests (the job passes connectors/ of both worktrees); per connector tool: new tool, lower class (read < write_reversible < external_effect < high_risk), changed action or executes_via -> widening, reverse -> narrowing; one fixture pair with golden report; /connectors/*/gxg-manifest.yaml in CODEOWNERS.

findings.problem: Tool name -> class map over all manifests: two manifests declaring x.msg.propose as high_risk and external_effect -> the later wins, auto_approve passes lint although the bundle holds a high_risk tool of that name (runtime still ignores it).
findings.required_improvement: duplicate tool name across manifests is a lint error (or keep the strictest class).

findings.problem: Arrival rule assumes (a) re-running an old run keeps created_at, (b) a head returns to an older SHA only with a force-push event. Case for (b): B ran 09:00, branch deleted and recreated at A, PR reopened, label 10:00, fast-forward to B 11:00 -> arrival 09:00 < label -> green. GitHub normally refuses such a reopen; not checked.
findings.required_improvement: Two owner checklist steps: re-run an old run and compare created_at; delete/recreate the head branch at another SHA and try to reopen.

findings.problem: Hand-written tools kept only to be dropped by build and warned about by lint (ignored-tools).

required_improvements: Finding 1: run the widening gate and gxg-policy from main's worktree; main-side gate requires the label when the PR touches gate paths (ci.yml, scripts/ci/, tools/gxg-policy/, schemas/, pyproject.toml, uv.lock); job test red for a PR that edits the gate with widening. Owner records in the plan the decision on the remaining `.github/workflows/` path (accept with 'owner reads such PRs', or org ruleset with a required workflow). Without that owner decision this is a plan/platform gap: stop and escalate.

Finding 2: manifest tool changes (new tool, lower effect_class, changed action/executes_via) reported as widening by gxg-policy diff and fed by grants_widening.sh from both worktrees; fixture pair with golden; connector manifests in CODEOWNERS.
Findings 3-4 (minor, do not block 9): duplicate tool name lint error; two owner checklist steps (re-run created_at, recreated branch reopen).
